beats.evidence: The Pandavas and Kauravas are cousins, Bhishma is their great-uncle and commands the Kaurava army, and Vyasa is grandfather to both lines.
The Ganguli English translation was published between 1883 and 1896.
Shantanu, Kuru king of Hastinapura, marries Ganga on the condition that he never questions her actions.
Ganga gives her first seven sons to the river; Shantanu stops her at the eighth, Devavrata, and she departs.
Satyavati's father demands that her son inherit the throne.
Devavrata renounces the throne and vows lifelong celibacy, earning the name Bhishma; Shantanu grants him the boon of choosing the time of his death.
Before marrying Shantanu, Satyavati bore Vyasa to the sage Parashara.
Shantanu and Satyavati's sons are Chitrangada, killed in battle, and Vichitravirya, who becomes king.
Bhishma wins the three princesses of Kashi; Amba is released, and Ambika and Ambalika marry Vichitravirya.
Vichitravirya dies childless; Bhishma refuses because of his vow; Satyavati calls on Vyasa.
By niyoga, Vyasa fathers Dhritarashtra (born blind as Ambika closed her eyes), Pandu (pale as Ambalika turned pale), and Vidura with a maid.

Dhritarashtra and Gandhari have a hundred sons, eldest Duryodhana, and a daughter Duhshala.
Gandhari blindfolds herself on learning Dhritarashtra is blind; Dhritarashtra has a son Yuyutsu by a maid, who later sides with the Pandavas.
Pandu marries Kunti and Madri; a sage's curse prevents him fathering children; Kunti holds a mantra from Durvasa to summon gods.
Kunti bears Yudhishthira (Dharma), Bhima (Vayu) and Arjuna (Indra); Madri bears Nakula and Sahadeva by the Ashvins.
Pandu dies with Madri under the curse; Madri ascends his pyre; Kunti returns with the five sons to Hastinapura.
Before marriage Kunti invoked Surya and bore Karna, whom she set adrift; he was raised by a charioteer and fights on the Kaurava side.
Karna is raised by the charioteer Adhiratha and his wife Radha, hence the name Radheya, and befriended by Duryodhana.
Kunti is the sister of Vasudeva, Krishna's father, making Krishna the Pandavas' cousin.
Arjuna wins Draupadi, daughter of Drupada of Panchala, at her svayamvara, and she marries all five Pandavas.
Pandavas and Kauravas are cousins; Bhishma is great-uncle to both and commands the Kaurava forces; Karna is the Pandavas' half-brother.
Tradition credits Vyasa as the composer of the Mahabharata; he is biological grandfather of both Pandavas and Kauravas.
